newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm, caution over US to prevail.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm, caution over US to prevail.

text.p: *Australian bonds took on a firmer tone following a modest rally in U.S. Treasuries and following a further local corrective sell-off on Monday.
*Market is likely to stay cautious ahead of key U.S. data.
Australian bonds took on a firmer tone following a modest rally in U.S. Treasuries and following a further local corrective sell-off on Monday.

"We're seeing a bit of a bounce this morning with the market looking a bit overdone on the downside yesterday. But we're probably close to the day's highs (on futures) already," said one trader at a European-based bank.

Market movements are likely to be tied to events in the U.S. over the next couple days in the absence of any major local data until the release of the first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings on Thursday.

A benign wages report, and weak outcomes to building approvals and retail trade data due on Thursday and Friday, could stir talk of another easing by the Reserve Bank, although for now the main view is that monetary policy is on hold for some time to come, analysts said.
The U.S. sees the first of its key data of the week later on Tuesday with the release of the first quarter employment costs index, along with March durable goods orders.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan is also due to address the International Monetary Fund/World Bank spring conference in Washington later on Tuesday.

Spread differentials to the U.S. were little changed, but they narrowed sharply to Canada amid continued weakness in the Canadian dollar. The fall was partly due to jitters over the June 2 Canadian election with Prime Minister Jean Chretien saying he may reverse some planned spending cuts.
